text:
maya: ran an extended perf pass comparing SM80 vs SM90 for paged+fused attention with the new dyn-batcher heuristic. seeing a consistent p99 spike on SM90 when KV cache churns during long prefixes.

cheng: can you paste the perf snippet and which CUDA/Triton builds you used? :eyes:

maya: here are the top lines from the run (trimmed):
```
model: gpt-j-6b
arch: sm90
kernel: flashx_paged_fused
cuda: 12.1
batching: dynamic (max_batch=32)
seq_len: 4096 (prefix heavy)
p50: 18ms
p95: 46ms
p99: 212ms  <-- regression vs sm80 (p99 ~95ms)
kv_cache_hit_rate: 78% overall, drops to ~40% during prefix flushes
mem_frag: +~16MB per stream on alloc churn
```

devon: that looks like KV warmup + fragmentation. the dyn-batcher currently delays prefill until batch>=8; with paged KV and long prefixes, delaying prefill means we do extra page pulls per request. try bumping kv_prefill threshold lower.

olga: interestingly, on SM80 the CUDA fused kernel path keeps steady latency at high seq_len. on SM90 the Triton fused variant shows higher latency under the same pattern. smells like allocator/backing-page differences between cudaMalloc/Trt memory pools.

ryan: did a microbench copying just the kv pull path across kernels. results: SM80 CUDA kernel: stable; SM90 Triton fused: stable until concurrent streams>6 then tail explodes. profiling shows many small cudaFree/cudaMalloc around token boundary.

maya: config I used for dyn-batcher: 
```
dyn_batch:
  max_batch: 32
  min_batch: 2
  queue_ms: 6
kv_policy:
  prefill_threshold: 8  # current
  page_backoff_ms: 0
```

devon: propose change: prefill_threshold -> 2, and add kv_prefill_hysteresis to avoid oscillation. Also fallback rule: if seq_len>2048 or kv_hit_rate<60% then route to cuda_direct kernel instead of triton_fused.

cheng: sounds good. can we get a quick A/B run? Want numbers for p99 and token throughput. make sure we test CUDA 11.8 and CUDA 12.1 variants.

bench-bot: scheduled ab_run_214222 for branches: dynbatch-prefill-lower, fallback-cuda-direct. runs queued on sm90-48g pool. ETA ~18m. :gear:

ryan: also instrumented allocator traces; attaching short excerpt: 
```
[trace] stream=3 alloc 2.1MB @ 0x7f...
[trace] stream=3 free 2.1MB
[trace] stream=3 alloc 3.0MB (new block)
[trace] stream=3 alloc 1.2MB -> falls back to large alloc path -> causes fragmentation
```
If we can switch Triton to use cuMemPool or set cudaMemAdvise it's likely to reduce fragmentation.

olga: note: switching memory backend has to be tested on SM80 too; we don't want regressions there. Also check cuBLAS/epilogue kernel selection differences across cuda versions.

maya: thanks — will run the A/B; initial hypothesis: lowering prefill threshold + route-to-cuda-direct fallback will remove p99 spike on SM90 with minimal throughput loss. will report back with bench-bot output and traces.

sre-bot: FYI deploy-watch: if A/B looks good we can roll the dyn-batcher change to dedicated pool and enable canary 5% traffic. will add rollback hook. :white_check_mark:

cheng: perfect. if bench numbers look clean I'll open a short PR with the heuristic changes + unit test for kv_prefill_hysteresis.

maya: added a TODO to the thread: 1) run CUDA 11.8 vs 12.1 on both arches; 2) microbench memory pools; 3) A/B p99+throughput; 4) prepare rollback plan.

bench-bot: ab_run_214222 completed: dynbatch-prefill-lower reduced SM90 p99 from 212ms -> 98ms, throughput -2.1%. fallback-cuda-direct path reduced p99 further to 90ms but added +3% cpu overhead. Full logs: https://bench.internal/214222_ab_run (internal)

maya: great, looks promising. will capture the perf trace and open a follow-up for kernel-selector heuristics so runtime picks memory-friendly kernel based on seq_len and kv_hit_rate.

cheng: thanks everyone. quick note — keep the Triton build pinned until we verify cuMemPool change.
